items.title: Existence of a bivariant class on a closed subscheme characterised by vanishing on the complementary component
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For two closed immersions i_1, i_2 covering X set theoretically, a perfect object E_2 on X_2 whose Chern classes are defined and whose restriction to X_1 cap X_2 is either zero or a finite locally free module of rank less than p in cohomological degree 0, the lemma produces a canonical bivariant class P'_p(E_2), respectively c'_p(E_2), in A^p(X_2 -> X) characterised by two capping properties: on i_{2,*}alpha_2 it returns P_p(E_2) cap alpha_2, respectively c_p(E_2) cap alpha_2, and on i_{1,*}alpha_1 it returns zero, with the same after any base change (statement lines 9694-9724). The proof writes an arbitrary class alpha' in CH_k(X') as i'_{1,*}alpha'_1 + i'_{2,*}alpha'_2 using the exact sequence for a cover by two closed subschemes, notes that alpha'_2 is well defined only up to an element in the image of the pushforward from X'_1 cap X'_2, and shows that setting P'_p(E_2) cap alpha' = P_p(E_2) cap alpha'_2 is independent of that ambiguity precisely because E_2 restricts to zero on the intersection (proof lines 9730-9742). In the rank case the same argument runs because c_p of the restriction vanishes by rank considerations (proof lines 9744-9748). Seeing that the only obstruction to well definedness is the ambiguity coming from the intersection, and that the two hypotheses are exactly what kills it, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
